title: As a painter of old Italy set his face in a dark corner of his canvas
html_source:
A convention in many paintings, both in those “of old Italy” and otherwise. Unclear to me if Joyce is referencing a particular painting. An example is Raphael’s face peeking out from behind a column in the large fresco “School of Athens”
https://mymodernmet.com/school-of-athens-raphael/

This passage also worked as support for Nabokov’s theory that the man in the macintosh in the Hades chapter and elsewhere in the novel was Joyce’s self-portrait.
